title: Four-stream chronological Bible plan — Psalm/Proverbs pairing review candidate

sourceMetadata.title: thiagobodruk/bible KJV structural dataset
sourceMetadata.use: Chapter and verse-count cross-check only; the candidate stores numeric metrics, never Bible wording. This public dataset is corroborative rather than a chronology authority.

sourceMetadata.title: Bible API World English Bible structural endpoint
sourceMetadata.use: Public-domain structural cross-check for 66-book identifiers and chapter boundaries; no wording is stored.

sourceMetadata.title: The Gospel Coalition, Introduction to the Old Testament
sourceMetadata.use: Confessional overview of the Protestant Old Testament's canon, genre, and ordering; the candidate labels its own chronological judgments as approximate.

sourceMetadata.title: The Gospel Coalition, Introduction to the Old Testament Historical Books
sourceMetadata.use: Confessional overview describing the rough chronological progression of Israel's historical books.

sourceMetadata.title: The Gospel Coalition, Introduction to the New Testament
sourceMetadata.use: Confessional overview noting that canonical New Testament order is not primarily chronological; this candidate therefore marks composition-based placements as approximate.

reviewNotes.old_testament: The event-order stream begins with the Pentateuch, proceeds through Israel's narrated history, positions prophets near their principal historical settings where practical, and labels uncertain placements as provisional rather than treating whole-book chronology as settled.
reviewNotes.new_testament: The stream preserves the Gospel-to-Acts narrative before a pragmatic, broadly composition-aware ordering of letters; several dates and relative orders remain disputed and are explicitly medium confidence.
reviewNotes.psalms: Psalms remain canonically ordered. Psalm chapters are paced primarily on Sundays; no individual historical superscription is treated as decisive enough to move a Psalm before review.
reviewNotes.proverbs: Proverbs ranges proceed canonically within one chapter at a time and are paired only with short Psalms. Their mechanical range boundaries require editorial review before activation.
